newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan NCB unveils details of new share issues.
newsitem.headline: Japan NCB unveils details of new share issues.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) on Tuesday unveiled details of a plan to boost its capital by 290.7 billion yen though new share issues.
The bank said in a statement that it plans to raise 167 billion yen by issuing ordinary shares and 123.7 billion yen by issuing preferred stock, both in third-party allotments.

The bank said private banks would buy 70 billion yen worth of the ordinary share issue and life and non-life insurers a total of 97 billion yen, the equivalent of about a half their outstanding perpetual subordinated loans to NCB.

It said a special fund set up by the government to deal with bad loans at failed housing loan firms, or "jusen", would buy 80 billion yen worth of the preferred stock issue and life and non-life insurers 43.7 billion yen worth.
The latter amount would be equivalent to a fourth of life and non-life insurers' outstanding subordinated loans to NCB, the bank said.
As a result of the new share issues, NCB's net assets per share would fall to 54.33 yen, down sharply from 216.16 yen as of the end of September last year, the bank said.
NCB said the terms of new shares would take into account future stock price movements.
It said its basic stance was that the terms needed to be set based on net assets per share, as well as financial markets' evaluation of NCB's financial strength and assets.
The terms must also be set in such a way that the bank's current shareholders will in effect shoulder the burden for the bank's losses, the bank said.
NCB said it wants to complete the capital increase as soon as possible after obtaining necessary approval from board and shareholder meetings.
